mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 6.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity and reduced business investment, which negatively impacts earnings and leads to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate regime, which erodes real corporate earnings and compresses valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and high interest rate regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-mo moving average in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month averages indicates robust labor market expansion, which increases consumer spending and corporate hiring, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by GDPC1 and RSAFS) for four consecutive months signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both decline for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during four-month declines in both GDPC1 and RSAFS.
